correctness.rationale: Source Algorithm 1 and Gaussian construction (7) give the exact scalar recurrence with chi-square-r Hessian denominator. Normalizing the initial sketched numerator yields an independent standard Gaussian Z, while each strictly oversized Gaussian gradient sketch contributes a positive chi-square c_j. The Z coefficient follows a degree-t polynomial whose leading coefficient is the nonzero product (-1)^t times all q_j c_j, and the extra-response remainder has degree at most t. Independent conditioning and a positive-probability bounded coefficient event prove both moment directions without cancellation, using exact chi-square inverse-moment integrability r>p(2t+1). The one-update formula is calculated from exact chi-square inverse moments. An independent standalone Python program replays the source recurrence and leading coefficients from real package paths.

value.rationale: IDS is specifically designed to trade gradient-sketch cost against accuracy while reusing a fixed Hessian sketch; unconditional robustness of its iterates is therefore a natural algorithm-design quantity. The exact all-p, all-finite-t threshold reveals a four-Hessian-row cost per optimization step for finite mean-square risk, even on a perfectly conditioned strong-convexity input. It explains a sharp discrepancy between existence of the sketched inverse, high-probability estimates, and unconditional moments, and identifies why increasing finite gradient sketch sizes cannot eliminate this heavy-tail phenomenon. The claim is a structural integrability boundary, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
